html:
Colombia is a country in northwest South America, the only one with coasts on both the Caribbean and the Pacific. Before the Spanish came, the Muisca farmed the highlands around Bogotá and the Tairona built towns such as Ciudad Perdida in the Sierra Nevada.

Spain ruled the land as New Granada, from 1739 the core of the Viceroyalty of New Granada. Bogotá declared self-rule in 1810, and independence was won at the Battle of Boyacá in 1819. After Gran Colombia broke up in 1830, the country changed its name and constitution several times, settling on the Republic of Colombia in 1886.

Its politics were marked by long fights between Liberals and Conservatives:

  • The Thousand Days' War of 1899 to 1902 killed tens of thousands.
  • In 1903 Panama broke away with American support, to build the canal.
  • Coffee became the great export in the early 1900s.
  • After the murder of the Liberal leader Jorge Eliécer Gaitán in 1948 came La Violencia, a decade of rural killing.

From the 1960s guerrilla armies such as the FARC fought the state. In the 1980s cocaine cartels, led by men like Pablo Escobar, waged war on judges and politicians. A peace deal with the FARC was signed in 2016. Colombia's best-known writer, Gabriel García Márquez, drew on this history of wonder and violence.
